title: Audit snapshot rotation and sealed retention playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement an operational playbook and automation to produce verifiable, residency-aware audit evidence for admin actions, access events, and configuration changes. The system must emit sealed snapshots (WORM-friendly) of admin activity with digest manifests, residency tags, and automated evidence exports for legal/compliance review. This ticket covers policy design, runtime hooks, storage orchestration, and ingestion automation for downstream evidence reporters.

Scope:
- Define snapshot cadence and rotation policy (hot -> sealed -> escrow) for admin audit data across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- Produce a signed manifest for each sealed snapshot containing residency metadata, retention policy ID, object digests, and key IDs used for encryption/signing.
- Implement an automated rotator service that: collects the current audit buffer, compacts events into a compacted snapshot (ndjson), computes chunk digests, signs the manifest with KMS/HSM-backed keys, uploads snapshot+manifest to WORM-capable storage (S3 Object Lock or on-prem immutable blobstore), and records the custody record in the evidence index.
- Add residency-aware placement rules: snapshots for EU customers must be sealed in eu-* regions only; S3 buckets must enforce region and object lock retention settings.
- Provide a retention-reconciliation job that enforces retention windows, rotates snapshots to long-term escrow (with separate key custody) and emits certificates of retention expiry for legal hold workflows.
- Expose audit-snapshot APIs for Console/Support to request on-demand sealed exports and to download signed manifests for audits.

Non-goals: full-text search over sealed snapshots, realtime ingest analytics (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Automated rotator produces sealed snapshots with signed manifests on a nightly cadence for all customers with admin audit enabled.
Sealed snapshots contain residency tag, retention policy ID, digest list, and signer key metadata; manifests are verifiable with our KMS public keys.
Uploaded snapshot objects have immutable retention enforced (S3 object lock or on-prem equivalent) and cannot be deleted before retention expiry.
Console shows per-customer sealed snapshot history and provides download links for artifacts plus signer verification details.
Retention-reconciliation job rotates >99% of eligible snapshots on schedule and creates escrow handoff events for legal hold cases.
Unit/integration tests for manifest signature verification and digest mismatch detection are present in CI.
Runbook for incident responders describing how to validate seals, re-generate manifests from raw audit buffers, and perform emergency escrow extraction is checked in.
tasks: Design manifest schema (fields: snapshot_id, start_ts, end_ts, residency, retention_policy_id, chunk_digests[], total_size, signer_key_id, signature, encryption_info)
Add audit-buffer compaction worker to transform event stream -> ndjson snapshot with deterministic ordering
Implement rotator service that computes chunk digests (SHA-256), uploads chunks, writes manifest, and triggers object-lock retention
Integrate KMS/HSM signing workflow with key rotation policy and signer audit trail
Provision WORM buckets and RBAC templates for eu/us/apac partitions and enforce placement rules
Console UI: sealed snapshot history page + download + verification view
Retention-reconciliation job that enforces expiry, creates escrow bundles, and integrates with legal-hold API
Add observability: per-snapshot latency/cost metrics, failure alerts, and manifest verification histogram
Write runbook and postmortem template for sealed snapshot failures
E2E tests: create events, force rotation, verify manifest signature and digest integrity
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff sync with Product and Security. Agreed to require KMS-backed signatures and residency tag enforcement. Decided to support both S3 Object Lock (hosted/dedicated) and on-prem immutable store (Private).
2026-02-20: Drafted initial manifest schema. Security requested inclusion of signer_key_id and key_version for future key rotation verification.
2026-02-24: Prototype rotator uploaded first snapshot to a dev S3 bucket with object lock enabled. Observed 2x overhead for chunk signing; need to batch digest ops and parallelize uploads.

2026-03-01: Compliance asked for a 'certificate of retention' artifact for each escrowed snapshot that includes retention start/end, legal-hold flags, and custodial handoff id. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-07: Design review with Infra: agreed to use SHA-256 digests and base64-encoded signatures. Decided to store manifests in a dedicated metadata prefix with ACLs mirroring the snapshot objects.

2026-03-10: Began implementation of deterministic ordering for the compaction worker to avoid nondeterminism across retries. Spike shows ordering by (timestamp, event_id) works for current stream schema.
notes: Migration considerations: existing audit archives must be backfilled into sealed snapshots for customers with retention policies > 1 year. Backfill will be a throttled job that preserves original timestamps and generates manifests referencing original raw-archive ids. Consider cross-account escrow for enterprise legal teams. Potential tradeoffs: longer rotation cadence reduces storage churn and signing cost but increases exposure window for mutable audit buffers.
